text: The effects of acid-base changes on cardiac output during diethyl ether anesthesia were studied in 25 mongrel dogs prepared by surgically implanting a plastic encased non-ferrous core electromagnetic probe on the ascending aorta. The findings are: (1) Metabolic acidosis produced only slight decreases in cardiac output but a more pronounced fall became evident with decreasing pH; (2) Respiratory acidosis led to a slight increase in cardiac output; (3) Respiratory alkalosis decreased cardiac output; (4) Metabolic alkalosis also produced a decline in cardiac output.
